newsitem.title: POLAND: UNIONS AT POLISH KGHM COPPER FIRM ON STRIKE ALERT.
newsitem.headline: UNIONS AT POLISH KGHM COPPER FIRM ON STRIKE ALERT.

text.p: Trade unions at Poland's copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA called on Thursday a strike alert after the firm's management failed to begin talks on pay demands and employment guarantees, a union official said.
Last week the seven trade unions active in KGHM said they wanted to launch a collective labour dispute with the company to press for their demands.

"We decided to go on strike alert because the management failed to show up at a meeting we planned to hold today on our demands," Jozef Czyczerski, the head of copper minining section of the Solidarity trade union, told Reuters.

Czyczerski said the union wanted pay increases matching at least the annual inflation rate, guarantees of employment for 10 years and keeping special minining industry privileges for all KGHM workers and pensioners.
"If the management refuses to start discussions we will follow with further actions which could include a warning strike," he said.
He added that the unions did not set any deadline for the talks to begin but expected the manangement to start talks soon.
"We did not set any firm date we expect the management will recognise that the situation is tense and will do something quickly," Czyczerski said.
He said the unions' demands were aimed at cushioning the impact of the restructuring of the firm which is earmarked for privatisation in the second half of this year.
Under Polish law a collective dispute is one of the stages to be gone through before a strike can legally be called but it need not necessarily result in a work stoppage.
